## R295-001: security-side closure

crates/tmux/src/control.rs:809-849 routes every open attempt through open_lock: O_NOFOLLOW, no truncation, and fd-based regular-file, current-UID, and single-link checks before chmod to 0600. No reopen bypasses those checks.

At 855-873, nonblocking try_lock is followed by comparing descriptor metadata with symlink_metadata(path), using BOTH device and inode. A mismatch or missing pathname releases the descriptor and retries; other metadata errors propagate. There are at most three total open attempts, including the first (809-824); exhaustion refuses with the typed AttachLockHeld/WouldBlock result. Real contention retains that result, while unrelated errors remain distinct (857-865).

The existing parent-directory guard (443-473) still selects a real directory owned by the current UID or root-plus-sticky, with no unsafe group/other write unless sticky, otherwise using the state-directory fallback. It runs before the reopen loop, not once per iteration. The file guards do run on every reopen. Prior directory-replacement residuals are not newly introduced protections.

Acquisition remains at control-client start before launch (647-651), not per successful read. No process launch was added by this recheck. The performance holder owns the final cost verdict.

## R295-002: no security regression

crates/testkit/src/tmux.rs:67-88 probes via in-process connect, with 10 ms sleeps and a two-second polling deadline. The implementation treats ConnectionRefused or NotFound as the server being gone. Success and unknown/permission errors do not authorize deletion. A refused connect is not unconditional proof of server death; see the named C34 follow-up below.

Failure to confirm termination returns Err before either unlink (99-108). finish_server reports failure by panic, or stderr when already unwinding (114-118). TestSession and LiveTmuxSession cleanup follows their existing teardown assertions (crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs:2317-2330; crates/daemon/src/pane_observer.rs:982-995). governance_boot still kills/reaps its owned foreground child before cleanup (crates/cli/tests/governance_boot.rs:212-218).

The actual unlink regression ran the real sweep --apply only inside its owned scratch directory. No live sweep was applied.

## Retained limits

No dynamic foreign-UID or three-consecutive-replacement exhaustion proof is claimed; those paths were source-checked. There is no dirfd/unlinkat anchoring. Prior sweep-directory validation and paired-socket metadata limits remain nonblocking notes, not new round-2 gates. C33 trusts same-user processes, not hostile other-UID manipulation; no new cross-UID exploitation path was established.

The cleanup deadline is checked between blocking connect calls; it is not a per-call timeout. The two-second claim is therefore a polling-deadline description, not a guaranteed wall-clock bound.

## New final-round boundary: C34 follow-up P295-R2-001

The correctness reviewer supplied an owned Darwin Unix-listener probe: backlog 1 with a queued connection returned errno 61/ConnectionRefused to a separate blocking connect; the same listener then accepted its queued client, exchanged data, and retained its socket pathname. This is an observed live-backlog counterexample to treating every refusal as death.

The implication for server_gone and the manual sweep is source-derived; no end-to-end unlink under this backlog schedule was demonstrated. Both original regressions and the scoped gates still pass. The reviewer has routed disposition to pm-001 under C34. Security records it explicitly, does not claim the untested boundary is safe, and does not create an independent third-round block.
